summary: Container with native scrolling and thin themed scrollbars. When the content overflows and an accessible name is present, it becomes a keyboard-focusable region.
whenToUse: Logs, long lists in fixed-height panels, horizontal filter rows on mobile.
whenNotToUse: For the whole page: let the document scroll.
Tables: Table and DataTable already handle horizontal overflow.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Maximum height (CSS length) beyond which it scrolls.

props.name: aria-label / aria-labelledby
props.description: Name of the region; required for it to become focusable when it overflows.

inherits: HTML attributes of the <div>; ref to the container.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the region (only if the content overflows).

accessibility: No scrollbar emulation: scrolling stays native (touch, wheel, keyboard, assistive technologies).
The region is focusable only when needed, to avoid adding unnecessary tab stops (WCAG 2.1.1).
responsive: Horizontal mode prevents page-level overflow on narrow viewports.
commonMistakes: Omitting aria-label: the overflowing region would not be reachable by keyboard.

examples.name: DynamicContent
examples.title: Growing content
examples.description: Comments are added with a button: the area becomes focusable only when the content overflows.

examples.name: BothDirections
examples.title: Scrolling in both directions
examples.description: Wide, tall grid with orientation="both" and a maximum height.

limits: Overflow detection uses ResizeObserver; without it, measurement happens only on mount and when children change.
